Definition: Churam, the name of an Israelite and two Syrians
BiblicalUsage: Huram is the name of a Benjamite in the genealogies and of the king of Tyre who sends cedar and craftsmen to Solomon. The Benjamite appears once in a list, and the king appears in the letters and the building of the temple. The name covers a nobody and a king, and both are remembered.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Huram of Tyre matters because a foreign king helped build God's house, and God uses outsiders for His work. The other Huram matters because God counts the Benjamites too.
